messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a spike in token-level latency for the EU cluster around 10:04 UTC. p50 fine but p95/p99 jumped ~2.3x for streaming routes. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/prod/inference/token-breakdown

perf-bot: ALERT: token_latency.p99 > 1.2s in eu-west for route=chat-stream (observed at 1760043200)

alex: I can pull a profile. Maria — is this only streaming or bookend synchronous gen too?

maria: Mostly streaming routes (chat-stream). Non-streaming gen route shows 10–15% increase but nothing like the tail.

jordan: Quick guess: kernel selector fell back to the generic matmul kernel for some sequence-length/quant combo. We saw similar tails in staging when selector misclassified 8k-range prompts.

chandra: I checked KV cache hit rate per-request — for the affected routes kv_cache.hit_rate dropped from 0.88 -> 0.62 for eu-west during the window. Cold cache + smaller batches could explain higher per-token overhead.

alex: attaching flame: ```
# pprof flat profile snippet
80.4s  25.1%  : runtime.select_kernel_generic
60.2s  18.8%  : aten.matmul_generic
25.1s   7.8%  : kv_cache::lookup_miss_path
12.0s   3.7%  : batching::emit_partial_batch
```

alex: also ran a query for per-route token breakdown (PromQL):
sum by(route,model_variant) (histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])))
-> shows chat-stream@v3 spiking in eu-west only

maria: That matches. But why only eu-west — same infra in us-west didn't have fallback. Any recent kernel selector changes deployed?

jordan: We rolled a selector tweak yesterday (commit 8f3a2) to handle micro-batches — it added a threshold that can misclassify sequences when quantized to int8. Might be triggering for models with mixed context lengths.

chandra: Also noticed routing policy: eu-west has a policy to prefer local pooled nodes with smaller batch windows (latency-focused), whereas us-west routes slightly more to shared nodes that sometimes have better kernel coverage. So different node images might explain deviance.

alex: Actionable telemetry gap: our dashboards don't currently break down token_latency by kernel label. We have route/model_region, but not kernel or kv_hit labels in the main panels. I propose adding panels for: 1) token_latency.p95/p99 by kernel 2) kv_cache.hit_rate by route+region 3) per-route avg batch_size and underfill ratio.

maria: +1. For routing policy metrics we should also show cross-region failovers and route decisions: counts of requests routed to fallback_model_variant or fallback_region with reason label (capacity|latency|error).

perf-bot: METRIC SUGGESTION: Add labels -> kernel, batch_size, kv_hit to token_latency and request_count metrics.

jordan: For quick mitigation I can revert the selector tweak on eu-west canaries or force toggle to prefer optimized kernels for int8. Which do we want?

chandra: Let's toggle selector to the old decision logic for eu-west canaries and monitor. If kv_hit is low we still need to improve cold-cache warmup (prefix caching improvement).

alex: I'll push a small dashboard PR and add the PromQL queries. Also adding an alert: if kv_cache.hit_rate drops >20% and token_latency.p99 > 1s in same window, fire a routed-traffic incident.

maria: Assigning: jordan -> selector toggle on canary (eu-west), alex -> dashboard + alerts, chandra -> investigate kv cache regression root cause (logs, prefetch failure). I'll watch the alerts.

deploy-bot: DEPLOYMENT started: rollback selector-tweak (commit 8f3a2 reverted) to canary eu-west at 1760043330 by jordan

jordan: Rolled back on canary — watching. Initial p99 down ~30% within one minute. Need longer window to confirm.

maria: Good signal. After 15m we should capture token-level histogram with kernel labels (newly added) to confirm hypothesis. If stable, schedule a targeted fix for the selector (dont misclassify int8 short sequences).

alex: Notes for dashboard PR: include panel for "route_kv_heatmap" showing kv_hit_rate vs avg_batch_size per route; add cross-region flow map for routing_decisions{route,from_region,to_region,reason}.

chandra: FYI logs show a small spike of prefetch errors in the canary nodes around the same timestamp — opening a storage ticket. Might be two contributing factors.

maria: Thanks all. I'll update the incident channel if anything escalates. For the metrics owners: let's try to ship the kernel-labeled token_latency metric by EOD so we can validate. :thumbsup:
